import importlib.util
print('pycosat', importlib.util.find_spec('pycosat'))
print('pysat', importlib.util.find_spec('pysat'))
print('z3', importlib.util.find_spec('z3'))

from pysat.solvers import Solver
from itertools import combinations
n=21
edge_index={}
vars=[]
k=1
for i in range(n):
    for j in range(i+1,n):
        edge_index[(i,j)]=k
        vars.append((i,j))
        k+=1
clauses=[]
# no red K4: each 4-set has at least one blue edge (var true=blue=1)
for S in combinations(range(n),4):
    clauses.append([edge_index[(i,j)] for i,j in combinations(S,2)])
# no blue K5: each 5-set has at least one red edge (var false) => negated
for S in combinations(range(n),5):
    clauses.append([-edge_index[(i,j)] for i,j in combinations(S,2)])
print('vars',k-1,'clauses',len(clauses))
with Solver(name='glucose3', bootstrap_with=clauses) as s:
    print('solving')
    sat=s.solve()
    print('sat',sat)
    if sat:
        m=s.get_model()
        vals=[1 if m[idx-1]>0 else 0 for idx in range(1,k)]
        print(len(vals))
        print(vals)
        # verify
        redK4=0; blueK5=0
        for S in combinations(range(n),4):
            if all(vals[edge_index[(i,j)]-1]==0 for i,j in combinations(S,2)):
                redK4+=1; print('redK4',S); break
        for S in combinations(range(n),5):
            if all(vals[edge_index[(i,j)]-1]==1 for i,j in combinations(S,2)):
                blueK5+=1; print('blueK5',S); break
        print('violations',redK4,blueK5)
